steps.content: At 7:30 in the morning, you and Pine arrive at the Shedde Town Municipal Office building, a full hour and a half before its official opening time.
At Pine's insistence, you've traded your signature gray coat—"too conspicuous," as she put it—for all-black attire and a dark baseball cap matching hers.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Tch, why is he here so early? I was planning to plant a bug on him during his morning commute...
Pine glares irritably at the only lit office upstairs. Through the spotless windows, you can see Hale already seated at his desk near the window, starting his day's work.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Forget about it. Let's set up the surveillance network first.
Pine pulls out a handful of devices from her pocket and jerks her head toward you.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You, plant these in his conference room, break room, and private office.
You look down and see an array of miniature surveillance equipment—cameras, listening devices, and similar gadgets—spread out in front of you.
How... how do I do this?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Tsk, what exactly are you good for anyway?

Pine shoots you a look of contempt, draws a launcher from her waist, and loads all the devices into it at once. Skillfully, she ascends a wall, clambers up a tree, and fires—each motion precise and practiced.
Within mere moments, those miniature devices are expertly placed in strategic, covert locations along the exterior walls and windowsills of the office building.
That was incredible... With skills like these, why not become a paparazzo? I bet no one in all of Eastside could dig up dirt better than you.

Despite having heard stories about her capabilities, witnessing these expert moves firsthand leaves you utterly stunned. Your jaw-dropped expression seems to amuse Pine, who responds with a knowing arch of her eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Who says I haven't been one?
Before you can process her words, Pine grabs your wrist and pulls you toward the central garden.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Come on, let's find a safe spot to monitor the surveillance.
The morning soon slips away, yet the results your surveillance has yielded turn out quite disappointing.

Helping injured field officers with their errands, visiting elderly residents in the community, volunteering at the animal shelter, organizing fundraisers for colleagues in need and receiving commendation banners in return...
Everything about Hale turns out to be these scattered acts of kindness, completely contradicting your initial profile of a desperate madman.

Pine clearly realizes this too. With a bare lollipop stick between her teeth and an increasingly furrowed brow, she keeps her eyes glued to the rapidly scrolling footage on her laptop screen, desperately searching for any crucial evidence to support her theory.
After much hesitation, you finally voice your thoughts in the most diplomatic way possible.
Pine, isn't it possible that Hale is simply an earnest person trying to do good? At least that's what our current evidence suggests, and his colleagues seem to think highly of him, too.
You mentioned he's publicly opposed many proposals from higher-ups, affecting their interests. Could it be that someone's seeking revenge by making an anonymous report to the Hedgehog's Eye?

You know the influence the Hedgehog's Eye carries, and your perspectives are... well, quite unique. Maybe someone's counting on you not investigating personally, using you as a tool to harm an honest young man. That's not impossible, right?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: For the Chief of MBCC to be this naive... I'm starting to worry about the Sinners under your command.
Pine lets out a contemptuous sneer and extends her arm, pointing directly at the office building across the street.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: See that building? All shiny windows and polished surfaces, but beneath them all lies nothing but a pit of mud. Once you step inside, you leave behind stains on your path that can never be scrubbed clean.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: And those who appear the most righteous? They're the truly terrifying ones! They scrub harder than anyone else to clean the mud from their shoes, desperate to keep others from catching the stench of their corruption when they get too close.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: I've seen plenty of pretenders in my time. Their masks always have cracks—just a little pressure and their true faces emerge. But Hale? He's different. I've never seen someone maintain such an airtight mask before.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Fascinating, isn't it?
Pine slams her laptop shut and clenches her fist, her piercing gaze fixed on the gleaming windows of the building across the street.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Even if the whistleblower is lying, I still need to see Hale's true face for myself and find out how he maintains such a perfect image!
Since the first interrogation, you've noticed that Pine's fixation on these people is different from those who simply chase clicks and fame.
Why is she so obsessed? What fuels her hatred? What did those in power do to her? What is she truly seeking?
Before you can voice your questions, Pine gathers her belongings and rises from the bench.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: If long-range surveillance doesn't work, then we'll switch to close-quarters tactics.

Equipped with Pine's tool kit and forged IDs, you both change into maintenance uniforms and slip into the building through the service entrance, making your way to the equipment room on the first floor without any resistance.

The reception room, separated from the equipment room by just a wall, is bustling with activity. To your surprise, besides the regular office staff, you spot numerous familiar faces from Eastside who've come for the pharmaceutical factory incident and Worthington, the supposed hero.
But what surprises you even more is Pine herself. Given her usual stubborn independence and perpetually impassive expression, you had long since mentally filed her away as "socially challenged."
You find it hard to believe that this is the same person—now she's gliding through crowds of strangers with a warm smile, effortlessly joining every conversation as if catching up with old friends.
Appearances can be deceiving, indeed...
Lost in thought, you suddenly feel Pine yanking your arm. At the same moment, something collides with your shoulder—
Oh! I'm so sorry. Are you hurt?
A young, familiar face appears before you, wearing an apologetic expression.
I'm fine...
You start to respond instinctively, but Pine moves faster, covering your shoulder and putting distance between you and the man—none other than Hale, your investigation target.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Sorry, sir. I wasn't able to keep him steady.
steps.female_content: Sorry, sir. I wasn't able to keep her steady.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: ...Oh, please don't worry. My friend just got a bit dizzy from low blood sugar. It happens from time to time—nothing a short rest won't fix.
Pine first gives Hale a polite smile, then takes your arm with warm concern as she speaks.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Let's get you some rest and something to eat, shall we?
While Pine's words are gentle, her grip is firm as she guides you towards the elevator. Hale gives you both an apologetic nod, still appearing guilty about the minor accident.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Nice work. Looks like you're good for something, after all.

Only when the elevator doors close does Pine release her grip on you, letting out a deep breath of relief. She pulls out a pair of miniature earpieces from her pocket, putting one on herself before fitting the other to your ear.
You made me bump into him on purpose so you could plant a bug on him?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: That's exactly why I said you're good for something after all.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: No one in the lobby knows anything useful about Hale, but I managed to get his office password. Let's go search his office thoroughly—might find something interesting. Once we're done, we'll take the staff elevator to B1 and slip out...
As Pine speaks, she pulls out a white keycard from her pocket and waves it in front of you with a mischievous grin.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Oh right, forgot to mention—I "borrowed" this from one of the cleaning staff just now.

The moment you step out of the elevator, your shackles detect Pine activating her special power. She becomes like a shadow melding with its surroundings, effortlessly concealing your presence along with hers.
She pulls you along through the bustling hallways, yet everyone passing by remains oblivious to your unfamiliar faces. Without a single interruption, you make your way straight into Hale's office.

After quietly closing the office door, Pine swiftly surveys the room. Her eyes dart from the decorative paintings on the wall to the hidden panels in the bookshelf and the desk drawers, mentally mapping every possible location where evidence might be concealed.
In one fluid motion, she pulls a black cloth from her toolkit and swings it over the security camera. Then, pointing at you, she lowers her voice.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Check the desk drawers for files, especially anything marked confidential. I'll handle everything else.

She crouches down by the safe in the corner, producing a thin wire and a stethoscope-like device before skillfully working on the lock. While you sort through the files in the drawers, you can't help but ask a question.
First climbing trees and pickpocketing, now cracking safes... Does everyone in your line of work need to learn such bizarre skills?
With a soft click, the safe door swings open. Pine pulls out a stack of documents, letting out a dismissive snort.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Hah, only paparazzi would know those tricks. No self-respecting journalist climbs trees.
You can't tell if she's being sarcastic or actually telling the truth.
Wait... were you actually a paparazzo?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Yeah, but who in their right mind would pick up that crappy job if they didn't have bills to pay... I actually wanted to be a political journalist at first, but things took quite a different turn.

Though Pine speaks casually, her words spark your curiosity. This is the first time she's voluntarily shared anything about her past, and these few sentences offer you a glimpse into who she used to be. You carefully pursue this line of conversation.
So, your interest in politics started pretty early?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: It wasn't really about interest at first. I just wanted to understand certain things.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Ever since I was a kid, I liked wandering around by myself, exploring every corner of the city. No real purpose to it—just passing time.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: But watching all these people hurrying about their different lives, I couldn't help but wonder—why did they live the way they did? So I started piecing together these fragments, trying to understand how the world really worked.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Eventually, being a mere observer wasn't enough to satisfy my curiosity. I began creating false identities for myself, infiltrating different social circles to experience their lives firsthand.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: But the deeper I dug, the more nauseating the truth became—the wealthy were duplicitous and scheming, the middle class numb and indifferent, the poor ignorant and malicious...

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: These completely different scums, despite their many conflicts, somehow found a way to coexist in society, each carving out their own territory while also keeping each other in line. I wanted to find out who was pulling the strings behind this system, so I set my sights on those at the top.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: They were DisCity's "guiding lights," always radiating brilliance on screen, spouting endless hope—making everyone believe they'd make the world a better place.
As Pine speaks, her words grow slower, and her expression darkens. Her gaze falls to the documents in her hands, fingers unconsciously tightening until the papers crumple beneath her grip.
...Pine, are you alright?
You approach carefully, not wanting to startle her. Keeping your voice low, you wait for her response.
After a long moment, Pine finally snaps out of it. She tosses aside the now-useless documents and manages a self-deprecating smile.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Back then, I thought that even though most of them were hypocrites peddling false hope to line their own pockets, surely someone would make the world better... Those far-off hopes always seem so enticing, don't they?

Before you can ask anything else, Pine suddenly raises her index finger, shooting you a sharp glance while mouthing "quiet." In one fluid motion, she crouches silently behind the desk and turns up the reception frequency on her headphones.

steps.speaker: Hale
steps.content: The person you mentioned... Yeah, I know what to do... Don't worry... later...

You also catch fragments of the conversation through the headphones. Before you can ask Pine about it, she has already pulled out a portable signal amplifier, expertly adjusting the frequency to capture Hale's call more clearly.
Her brow furrows slightly, her concentration as intent as a surgeon's during a precise operation, completely shutting out all external distractions.

Unfortunately, the building's signal blocking proves too effective—before you can make out the details of the conversation, the call ends with a click, followed by footsteps echoing through the headphones. The crowd noise gradually fades as Hale exits the building.

After confirming through the window that Hale has gotten into a taxi, Pine packs away her equipment and swiftly returns everything in the room to its original place. Her movements flow with the grace of a trained operative—fluid, swift, and precise.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: He left alone. Come on, let's tail him.

The tracker leads you to a dilapidated alley. The ground is muddy, strewn with moss. With its remote location, decrepit infrastructure, and complete lack of surveillance cameras, this seems like the perfect spot for shady dealings.
You follow Pine, carefully picking your way through the treacherous ground deeper into the alley. Soon enough, you hear Hale's familiar voice ahead.

steps.speaker: Hale
steps.content: ...Please, I insist you take this money.
Is he finally showing his true colors? You exchange a glance with Pine before carefully peering around the corner toward the source of the voice.
Contrary to your expectations, the person standing opposite Hale isn't some high-ranking official, wealthy businessman, or fugitive criminal—but a white-haired elderly man with a hunched back.

steps.speaker: Old Man
steps.content: I've already told you, I can't accept this money. How many more times do I have to say it?

steps.speaker: Hale
steps.content: Your son gave his life for Shedde, and the compensation you received doesn't align with what was publicly promised—that in itself was unjust. I hope you can find some peace and at least use this money to move out of this alley.

steps.speaker: Hale
steps.content: Your granddaughter will be starting school soon. Living here without even an air conditioner—it's too much for both you and the child to bear.

Finally, the elderly man silently accepts the money and gestures for Hale to join him for tea inside. Hale gladly accepts, and their figures disappear one after another behind the dark curtain of the doorway.
Pine... should we continue investigating Hale?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Is that even a question? Of course we continue. One good deed isn't enough to clear him of suspicion.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Besides, this is clearly all an act—I've seen it too many times... He's probably got cameras hidden somewhere already, ready to capture footage of the "selfless model officer in action" for his own promotion.

Pine's gaze remains fixed on where Hale has disappeared, her stance unyielding, determined to pursue this to the bitter end. In her worldview, it seems impossible for anyone within the circles of power to be genuinely good.
Pine, I'm not trying to convince you that Hale is a good person or anything like that. I just think we could try looking at this from a different angle—

Let's set aside whether Hale is truly a hypocrite or not—his actions are at least bringing some relief to the victims' families. If this anonymous tip-off succeeds, we won't even see these orchestrated acts of kindness anymore.
So wouldn't you say that, compared to Hale, this anonymous informant might be the bigger problem?
Pine narrows her eyes and turns to face you with keen interest.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Go on.

Let's break down the potential motives of the informant. One: Hale is genuinely corrupt, and the informant is either his victim or someone who couldn't stand by watching his misdeeds. Two: Hale is actually innocent, but he's hurt someone's interests, and the informant is among those affected—in which case, all this evidence is fabricated to frame him.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: To frame him...
Pine mutters to herself, lost in thought.
Based on our firsthand investigation findings, I personally lean toward the second possibility. What do you think?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Interesting.
Pine gives a slight smile, her eyes showing approval.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You do have a point there. I didn't expect bringing you along would actually prove useful.
Having reached an understanding with her, you let out a sigh of relief.
In that case, let's head back to MBCC to plan our next move. I'll have our intelligence team trace the source of that message you received...
Before you can finish your sentence, Pine cuts you off.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: No need. We've already got a prime suspect right here who's worth looking into.
You mean... Worthington?
Pine gives a decisive nod.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: We discussed this before—if Worthington were to fall from grace, Hale would benefit the most since he'd be the prime candidate to take over as Shedde's Town Councilor.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: But let's look at it from another angle: now that Worthington's getting promoted, his position will be vacant too. Someone like him would surely want to maintain his grip on Shedde. So among all his subordinates, who would be the last person he'd want as his successor?
...Hale.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: The tip-off clouded my judgment. That's why I made the mistake of viewing Worthington as a passive player in all this... Hah, since when has he ever been passive about anything?
Pine lets out a cold scoff, her voice carrying its usual caustic mockery, but now tinged with barely contained hatred.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: That blood-stained bastard always manages to mask himself with integrity and altruism. After all these years, he's still pulling the same dirty tricks—framing others and climbing the ladder by stepping on everyone in his way...
She jerks her head up, her eyes blazing with a cutting fury, her voice sharp enough to send chills down one's spine.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Those people he crushed might have thought they were finished. But too bad for him—I'm still here. And I'll make him pay for everything he owes, down to the last debt!

You hesitate, your eyes darting between Pine's stone-cold expression and her clenched fists. Her demeanor seems even sharper than usual, and this obvious emotional surge makes you wonder if there's more to the story.
...Pine, your attitude towards Worthington seems to be more than just your typical disdain for his kind.
You carefully phrase your question while studying her expression, trying to glean more information from her reaction.
Did you know each other before? Is there some history between you two?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Hah, it goes far beyond just some history.
With a cold laugh, she yanks off the necklace from her neck—beneath the black band lies a faint but unmistakable scar stretching across her throat.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: It's a blood feud.

steps.speaker: Paparazzo A
steps.content: Hey, did you hear? Pine topped the readership rankings again this month! It's so frustrating—she's barely out of college, just some rookie girl, and she's getting these incredible numbers?

steps.speaker: Paparazzo B
steps.content: Don't be so jealous. Like the editor-in-chief says, some people are just cut out for this job. Look, she just secured another hefty hush payment for the company. Our bonuses this month are all thanks to her.

Meanwhile, in a corner of the room, the girl who has been the subject of office gossip slouches wearily in an uncomfortable chair. On her monitor played the day's political news, creating a stark contrast with her work notes sprawled across her desk—a chaotic mess of papers.

Who was having a secret relationship, who was committing fraud, who was splurging at luxury boutiques for their new flame... The pages were filled with notes about vapid celebrities and their even more vapid daily lives.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: It's all just petty, mind-numbing, disgusting nonsense, draining my brain, wasting my time... Why am I even here, churning out trash like some machine...
With a sigh, she buries her face in her hands, utterly dejected.

Across the papers, beyond the celebrity gossip, several connecting lines led to other notes detailing how Eastside's bigwigs lined their pockets with embezzled funds, traded favors for sexual bribes, and lived lives of endless debauchery... Their supposedly noble cause of "leading DisCity towards a better future" was nowhere to be seen from their actions.
Suddenly, the news broadcast was cut off.

steps.speaker: Newscast
steps.content:
Breaking news:

We have received confirmation that the renowned actress Liz was discovered deceased in her residence at 5:45 this afternoon. Police have secured the scene. Preliminary investigation indicates the cause of death as sudden cardiac arrest, with time of death estimated at early this morning.
Please stay tuned for further updates...

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: What...? She's dead?

Pine jolted upright, her hands flipping back through her notes until they landed on a particular page where Liz's name stood out. The very same woman now being reported dead had paid Pine's company a substantial sum just days ago to bury a story.

From Liz's name on the page, a striking red line extended outward, linking directly to Vick, the Town Councilor of Shedde who had been making frequent appearances in Eastside lately, rumored to be on the fast track for promotion.

While investigating Liz's private life, Pine stumbled upon her secret relationship with Vick. Just another politician-celebrity liaison—nothing surprising—so Pine had simply saved the footage of their argument from last night to her memory card without giving it much thought.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: A healthy person with a normal lifestyle, no recent acting jobs to stress over—how does someone like that just drop dead from "sudden cardiac arrest"? This was no accident. The person at her house last night had to be...
The newscast had already moved on to international coverage. Even the death of a public figure, it seemed, wasn't worth more than a moment of people's attention.
But Pine's blood was racing as the red line in her notebook seemed to come alive, weaving through her mind and connecting all the scattered pieces of evidence—
She straightened up and started writing with an intense fervor.

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: ...What is this garbage? "Rising Political Star's Murky Ties to Deceased Actress"? You might as well openly accuse him of murder! There's no way we can publish this. You have three days to write something new.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Why?! This is all first-hand evidence from my own investigation, and everything in this article comes from my own leads. How can you just throw it out like this?!

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: Evidence? This is nothing but speculation! You're a journalism graduate from a respected college. Don't you realize that reporters must uphold professional integrity and ethical standards? And here you are, throwing around baseless accusations!
As Pine listened to this sanctimonious lecture about journalistic integrity, she could only marvel at the sheer absurdity of it all.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Now you lecture me about evidence and ethical standards? Where was all this talk about journalistic integrity and objectivity when you had us stalking celebrities and fabricating trashy tabloid stories for clicks?!

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: You...! Do you have any idea who you're trying to smear?! Do you know how much influence Vick has right now?! You'll bring us all down with you over a trivial piece of truth!

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Hah, now we get to the truth! You're too scared to challenge someone powerful, so you'd rather bury the story and turn a blind eye. And you expect me to do the same? Keep dreaming!

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: I'm not forcing you—this is just how the world works! If you want a normal life, you need to learn when to look the other way. Especially in this industry, what you know isn't always what you see, and what you see isn't always the truth.
Seeing Pine unfazed with her arms crossed, the editor softened his tone. His expression shifted to one of concern, though a veiled threat lurked beneath his words.

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: ...Tell you what—I'll pay you a nice sum to write something more... appropriate. Remember, you're just a fresh graduate with an average degree and no connections in this industry. I might be your only shot at staying employed.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Is this coming from you, or from Vick?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You took his hush money, and now that I won't play along, you're generously offering me a cut to keep quiet? I'll say it again—keep dreaming.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: I quit.

With those final words hanging in the air, Pine stormed out, slamming the door behind her. She strode down the hallway past her stunned colleagues, pushing through the office's main entrance—all while completely ignoring the editor-in-chief's furious shouts.
A world of possibilities unfolded anew before Pine as she stepped outside, the fresh breeze carrying with it the promise of freedom and the chance to pursue her ideals.
After leaving the news company, Pine divided her time between investigating the actress' death and tracking Vick's every move, determined to uncover evidence of his corrupt dealings.
However, having learned from his past mistakes, Vick had become far more cautious, bringing Pine's investigation to a standstill.
Then, on a stormy night, Pine's email notification chimed—an anonymous message appeared in her inbox with an attachment coming along.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: "The thing you're investigating"... What kind of strange email title is that?
Despite her suspicions, Pine decided to download the file.

10%, 40%, 90%... The moment the download was completed, the file self-extracted, filling the screen with photos of Vick at various underground establishments. Dozens of video files lined the bottom of the window, along with contact information.

Pine arrived at the meeting spot right on time. The cafe is empty save for a single customer—a man sitting by the window, calmly reading his newspaper. After a moment's hesitation, Pine approached him cautiously.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Are you... the one who contacted me?
Yes, that's right. Miss Pine, pleased to meet you. Please, have a seat. You actually came to meet me... I see I wasn't wrong about you.
The man rose with a smile to shake Pine's hand, then guided her to the seat across from him with practiced courtesy. His every gesture exuded an air of warmth and reliability.

Now then, time is short, so let's cut to the chase—Miss Pine, I know what you've been working on. I greatly admire your efforts, and I wanted to help. That's why I sent you all the evidence in my possession...

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Hold on... Who are you? And how do you know about all this?
Pine cut him off with a frown, and the man responded to her wariness with a slightly apologetic smile.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Ah, my apologies. I got ahead of myself—I'm Worthington, an administrative officer in Shedde Town, and I happen to be Vick's subordinate... as well as his student.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Student?

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Yes, I've worked under him since graduating college. He taught me that we must act with integrity and live with honor, never yielding to temptation. Only then, he said, could we give our people hope for tomorrow and build a better future.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: I idolized him and lived by his every word, until one day... I stumbled upon his secret and finally realized he was nothing but a hypocrite who preached virtue while practicing vice.
A wry smile crossed Worthington's face, his voice tinged with bitter resignation.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: I tried to convince Vick to stop his wrongdoing, but he just mocked me for being naive. From that day on, I lost his trust and found myself pushed aside in every way possible.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: All these years, he's played his political games and climbed to great heights, while I remain just a minor commissioner with nothing but the scraps of evidence I've managed to gather...

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: So you came to me, hoping I'd help expose him? But why now, of all times? I don't even have a platform to publish anymore—I just quit my job, and I'm sure you know that.
Worthington took a deep breath, his gaze fixed on Pine with sincere determination.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: I admit, it was my own cowardice that kept me from exposing this evidence. But it wasn't until that lady's death that I finally realized—if Vick continues unchecked, more and more innocent people will be dragged into this.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Yes, I came to you hoping you would help me with this. I know you've left the news company, and I know why. In fact, that's exactly what motivated me to take the risk of seeking your help.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Because you're someone with a true sense of justice. You can't be bribed, you won't yield to threats or temptation, and above all, you won't compromise your own principles.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Can you forgive my past cowardice and join me in overcoming this challenge? I believe together we can turn empty promises into real action. Starting now, at the very least!
In that moment, Pine felt her blood surge with renewed passion.

Her heart resonated with his words, and she found herself unable to resist believing in the person before her. Perhaps in this broken and chaotic world, there were still those who stood righteous, persistently bringing hope to everyone.
After their conversation, Pine returned to her apartment and spent three days meticulously compiling Worthington's evidence into a scathing report, each line a damning indictment of Vick's misdeeds.
The moment the article went live, Vick found himself at the center of a firestorm. Despite his vehement denials, the overwhelming public outcry caught the attention of the Public Security Bureau.
When Pine learned that Vick had been taken in for questioning and would soon face sentencing, her heart pounded in her chest, racing with the gravity of the moment.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Finally... I've finally done it...

The young woman murmured to herself as she collapsed onto her bed. She hadn't properly rested for days, constantly monitoring the article's analytics and public response. Now, at last, she could close her eyes and drift into peaceful dreams.
Sometime later, the morning news announced Vick's arrest and imprisonment on multiple charges. However, as Pine carefully read through the list of allegations, the blood drained from her face.
The remote slipped from her grip, batteries scattering across the floor. Finally coming to her senses, she reached for her phone with trembling hands and dialed Worthington's number.
It was another rainy night. The young woman sat motionless in the cafe, the storm outside matching the turmoil in her heart.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: The evidence you gave me was all fake, wasn't it? You came to me with fabricated evidence when I was desperate to prove my worth!

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You knew someone like me, with no connections, had no way to verify the evidence. All I could do was trust your word, only to be exploited as your pawn to bring down your superior and clear your path to promotion!
In stark contrast to Pine's outburst, Worthington remained perfectly at ease. He reclined on the sofa, hands folded over his knees, watching the furious young woman with calculated composure.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: So what if the evidence was fake? He was never a good person to begin with. You know full well what he's done.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Pine, this isn't exploitation—it's a mutually beneficial arrangement. I provided an opportunity, and you helped me solve a problem and got your chance to prove your worth. Isn't that the perfect outcome?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: How could you do this?! How could you use fabricated evidence to make me do your dirty work?!

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: You know full well that without the evidence I provided, you could never have written that article, let alone put him behind bars. Your dreams, everything you wanted to prove—none of it would have been possible.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Without my fabricated evidence, you'd still be nobody but an unemployed college graduate, sitting in some cheap apartment worrying about how to pay your utility bills.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: But you're not a student anymore, Pine. This is how the real world works—the end justifies the means. We used fabricated evidence to draw an investigation, which led us to real evidence, and he got the punishment he deserved.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: You see what this is, right? Different approaches, same outcome. Essentially, we both achieved the same goal—eliminating a threat to society, didn't we?
His rushed tone gradually steadied itself.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: Pine, you're incredibly talented, but your potential has been wasted all this time. Others may be blind to it, but I see what you're truly capable of.

steps.speaker: Worthington
steps.content: This collaboration has only reinforced my belief that I chose the right person. I want you to work with me—together, we can pursue what we believe is right.

Pine found herself at a loss for words, perhaps because there was nothing left to say. As she watched this ambitious man climbing the rungs of power with such vigor, she was surprised to find only an infinite calmness settling in her heart.
Suddenly, the Worthington before her seemed like a stranger. He appeared different from all the others on the surface, yet somehow, he was exactly the same.
But wasn't everyone just the same in the end? This world, and every single person in it. No exceptions, no one spared.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: You're right. This is just how the real world works. I should thank you for teaching me such a valuable lesson—"the ends justify the means." Truly... enlightening.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: But I'm afraid your only companion on this path will be the one already behind bars, not me—because one day, I'll personally make sure you end up right there with him.
Pine rose to her feet and cast one last impassive glance at the man who sat there, perfectly composed in his arrogance.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Our approaches are different, and so are our outcomes. This is our last meeting.
Then?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Then, someone slit my throat on my way home. Lucky for me, I awakened as a Sinner just in time—that's the only reason I'm standing here talking to you now.

Pine's tone remains as abrasive and irritating as ever, but you find yourself quietly relieved. An increasing certainty settles within you that she isn't the unprincipled, irresponsible person she appears to be. Perhaps in Pine's heart, there has always been a delicate balance—a scale that never stops weighing right and wrong.
If you two are done chatting, perhaps it's time to show yourselves?
A familiar voice cuts through the air, and you both suddenly realize that Hale has emerged beside you, unnoticed until now.

steps.speaker: Hale
steps.content: No need to be so surprised. After all, you're not the only ones who know how to use these gadgets.
He leans against the wall, pointing to the blue-lit earpiece on his ear. Pine pulls open your coat and feels around, unsurprised to find a tiny listening device tucked away in your pocket.
Was it when we bumped into each other in the lobby...?

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Heh, seems you're not as stupid as we thought. We underestimated you.
Pine lets out a quiet laugh and carelessly tosses aside the listening device. Then, she walks straight up to the man and candidly reveals both her identity and purpose.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: The Hedgehog's Eye received an anonymous tip accusing you of multiple crimes, including abuse of power, financial fraud, and orchestrating the pharmaceutical factory explosion.

steps.speaker: Pine
steps.content: Based on our investigation, we believe your superior, Worthington, is likely behind the tip. After looking into the conflicts between you two, he's emerged as our prime suspect.
After hearing Pine's words, Hale's face shows no trace of surprise. He shakes his head thoughtfully.

steps.speaker: Hale
steps.content: I'm aware of this... but Worthington isn't behind it.
Do you know who the whistleblower is?
Hale looks at you both and gives a slight nod, an unexpected smile slowly spreading across his face.

steps.speaker: Hale
steps.content: It's me.
